messages:
maria: Heads-up — putting together a short playbook for the offline/orchestrator upgrade flow. Focus is on making interrupted upgrades resumable and operator-friendly. Wanted quick sanity-checks on the checkpointing granularity and abort/rollback semantics.

alex: +1 on resumability. prefer manifest-level checkpoints (not just file offsets) so we can resume after reboots without replaying entire graph.

kevin: agree. also: need an explicit apply marker per component. if apply(id) recorded, skip on resume. avoids partial-apply pitfalls.

sylvia: tradeoff: more markers = more metadata we need to persist and ship. what's our persistence surface? local disk for short-term + signed resume token in control-plane?

maria: proposal: local level: per-agent apply journal (append-only), per-bundle checkpoint including manifest digests and applied components. control-plane: resume token that contains last-accepted manifest digest + nonce + HMAC.

tim: that HMAC token is nice for ops UX. operator sees token in UI/CLI and can hand it to support to resume. but must be revocable if operator aborts.

jen: revoke semantics are important. If operator aborts mid-apply we should mark the job as cancelled and emit a cancellation marker that prevents auto-resume. manual resume requires an explicit --force flag and new token.

kevin: question: how do we handle partial-file/corrupt chunks? e.g., transfer stopped during chunk 23 of 120. Resume should start from chunk 23, but we also need a way to validate chunk integrity quickly.

alex: keep a per-chunk checksum in the manifest. agent verifies checksum on receive, writes chunk. On resume, agent requests missing chunk ranges and verifies. If checksum mismatch, agent purges the partial and redownloads range.

maria: note: avoid re-downloading already-applied components. applied components are immutable and verified by digest. If digest matches, skip.

sylvia: operationally we also need visibility: expose endpoint /api/v1/upgrades/<job>/status that returns checkpoints, applied components, last-chunk, and suggested next-step. UI should show "resume" / "abort" buttons.

tim: CLI UX sketch: 
```
# show job status
rictl upgrade status --job 8a3f
# resume job
rictl upgrade resume --job 8a3f --token 3f2e --force
# abort job
rictl upgrade abort --job 8a3f
```

jen: +1. Also: provide a dry-run resume mode so we can validate manifests and checksums before actually writing to system dirs. Operators will love that.

kevin: one more: KV-cache and runtime state. If a model-serving process is active, upgrade should capture a memory-drain window: drain incoming traffic, snapshot state, then activate new artifacts. If resume occurs mid-drain, we need to detect and either retry drain or fallback to warm-start.

maria: good call. add a "drain-checkpoint" step in the orchestration graph; agent records pre-drain state and post-drain marker. resume semantics: if pre-drain recorded but post-drain missing, we re-run drain step.

alex: security: signed manifests + optional per-operator approval step for enterprise. resume token must include operator id for audit.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Upgrade job 8a3f created by jen at 2026-03-19T14:02Z. Status: downloading (45%).

jen: tiny nit: make sure resume tokens expire after a configurable TTL to avoid long-lived tokens lying around. default 72h?

maria: noted. default TTL 72h, cluster-admins can extend. Also add an auto-cleanup policy for abandoned jobs.

sylvia: can we avoid too many on-disk markers to reduce write amplification on embedded devices? maybe use a single compact journal with protobuf entries instead of many small files.

kevin: agreed, single journal + periodic compaction works. journal entries: {seq, step, digest, marker, timestamp, signature}.

maria: rough next steps: 1) draft playbook document with state machine (manifest-checkpoint, chunk-apply, component-commit, drain, activation, cleanup) 2) prototype resume token format + CLI flags 3) add /status API + UI mock 4) run tabletop with support & SRE.

alex: happy to pair on the prototype token format.

jen: I can take the UI mock and CLI copy.

tim: I can write the agent append-only journal prototype and compaction job.

maria: thanks all. will drop an initial draft in #docs/rfc later today, pinging @alex @jen for review. :thumbsup:
